generated_from: manual code + test inspection this round (grep + read, see chat record), prepared per the Round 7 work order's §II requirement to make the system ready for an external pentest to start immediately
purpose: This inventory does not replace an independent penetration test -- it exists so a real external vendor can start immediately against a documented surface, and so this program can honestly show what adversarial coverage already exists internally versus what a vendor should specifically focus new attention on.

categories.evidence: pkg/api.Gateway.Handle is the single production entrypoint every capability routes through; pkg/api.Registry.Declare/BindREST/BindGRPC/VerifyParity enforces that every declared capability is bound and REST/gRPC surfaces stay in parity (TestParityViolationIsDetectedInBothDirections).
pkg/api.Verifier: RS256 JWT verification, alg=none refusal, unknown-kid refusal, issuer/audience/expiry/not-before enforcement, malformed-token refusal.
pkg/authz.Engine: versioned, signed, approved policy Documents with Rule/Condition-based RBAC+ABAC evaluation (Can/DryRun/Explanation), relationship-based (ReBAC) checks via Relate/hasRelation.
pkg/insurance/caseroom.Authorize/AuthorizeContext: tenant, jurisdiction, and scope matching, fail-closed on any mismatch, chained into the Golden Cross-Domain Case.
Cross-tenant and cross-jurisdiction access are both explicitly adversarially tested against the real golden case, not a synthetic fixture.
Delegation chain depth is policy-limited (default 5) and enforced at registration time; self-delegation and over-depth chains are refused.
Both revoked and expired relationships are proven unable to act, against the real golden case.

Idempotency-key replay is explicitly tested (same key/same payload replays the stored result; same key/different payload is a conflict; concurrent in-flight use is refused, not double-executed); cold replay of the whole golden case (including Case Room authorization) is proven identical to the live run.
Tampered evidence artifacts are refused rather than degrading silently; tampered release-certificate signatures are detected; tampered axis evidence degrades to FAIL rather than passing.
Malformed JWTs are refused at the verifier; broader malformed-input handling is exercised across the acceptance adversarial suite.
grep for a dedicated SQL-, command-, or path-injection test targeting pkg/api or pkg/insurance/* endpoints found none beyond pkg/blockers/pentest's own probePathTraversal.
categories.gap_note: VERIQO's own zero-external-dependency, stdlib-only architecture means there is no SQL layer to inject into, which narrows this risk considerably, but command/path-injection surfaces (e.g. any file-path or shell-adjacent input) are not yet covered by a dedicated adversarial test beyond the one path-traversal probe. Worth a real pentest vendor's explicit attention.

categories.evidence: grep for 'SSRF' anywhere in the repository returns zero matches. VERIQO's live-data connectors (pkg/connector/aisstream, pkg/connector/bol, pkg/connector/sar, pkg/connector/insurance, pkg/connector/payment) fetch external URLs, which is exactly the kind of surface SSRF controls (URL allow-listing, no-redirect-to-internal-address checks) would need to cover.
categories.gap_note: A genuine, honestly disclosed gap: no SSRF-specific control or test exists yet on the connector layer. Recommended as an explicit pentest scope item, and a good candidate for internal engineering closure before the external test (add an allow-list + private-address-block check to the shared connector HTTP client).

categories.evidence: Token-bucket rate limiting with per-tenant/actor/endpoint isolation, per-endpoint rule overrides, and deterministic behavior; the Gateway itself is proven to reject BEFORE consuming rate budget (so a rejected request cannot itself be used to exhaust the budget) and returns 429 correctly.
Token issuer/audience/expiry/not-before are all enforced; a tampered payload fails signature verification even with an otherwise well-formed token.

internal/timestamp provides a hash-chained, tamper-evident notary chain for release certificates; pkg/platform/audit exists and is used by cmd/veriqo-node/cmd/veriqo-gateway/pkg/workflow. However (see INSURANCE_COMPLETENESS_AUDIT.json, GAP-AUDIT-SUBSYSTEM-NOT-UNIFIED), the insurance domain's own dossier audit trail is not wired to pkg/platform/audit, so audit-log integrity is proven for the platform layer but not yet unified across the insurance domain.
categories.gap_note: See GAP-AUDIT-SUBSYSTEM-NOT-UNIFIED in FINAL_MASTER_GAP_MATRIX.json for the full account.

categories.evidence: A real authz wildcard-escalation probe exists and passes; RBAC role enforcement at the Gateway is directly tested; sandbox-level OS enforcement is separately tested.
Rate limiting (token bucket, per-tenant isolation, 429 on limit) plus the stress_slo readiness gate's own sustained-load SLO measurement.
Telemetry export leakage is explicitly tested (secrets must never reach an exported telemetry event); platform security and sandbox enforcement both have their own dedicated test suites.
